questions.question: The Viceroy Lord Curzon partitioned Bengal in _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1905.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Lord Curzon was the Viceroy of India from 1899 to 1905.
 
• The partition of the Bengal province came into effect during his viceroyalty on 16th October 1905.
 
• The idea of using the Bengal partition as a political tool to undermine the growing nationalism in Bengal.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• As per Curzon, after the partition, the two provinces would be Bengal (including modern West Bengal, Odisha, and Bihar) and Eastern Bengal and Assam.
 
• Bengal would have a Hindu majority and Eastern Bengal and Assam would have a Muslim majority population. Its capital would remain Calcutta.
 
• Many people in Bengal regarded this partition as an insult to their motherland. 
 
• Rabindranath Tagore composed the famous song ‘Amar Sonar Bangla’ which later became the national anthem of Bangladesh.
 
• Muslims led by the Nawab Sallimullah of Dhaka supported the partition.

questions.question: The snake boat race is a unique feature of which of the following festivals?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Onam.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Boat races of Kerala are a special feature of Onam.**
 
• Onam is the **harvest festival** **of Kerala** which is celebrated to welcome King Mahabali.
 
• Depending on the Malayalam Calendar, the festival falls in the month of** August or September **and lasts for **4-10 days.**
 
• Celebrations involve songs, dance, games, and feasts.
 
• **The Snake Boat Race called Vallamkali **is carried out on the** Pampa river** with hundreds of people racing and chanting folk songs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kalinga Festival**

 
 
• ​**Kalinga Mahotsav** is one of the most famous festivals of** Orissa.**
 
• It holds great religious significance for people.
 
• The aim of this festival is **to encourage people to follow the path of peace and calm,** rather than fighting amongst themselves.
 
• The** Vishwa Shanti Stupa,** also called the Peace Pagoda, serves as the **venue **of the Kalinga Mahotsav.
 
 
 
• **Bhogali Bihu**
 
 
• ​Magh Bihu or Bhogali Bihu is a **celebration of bountiful nature and abundance.**
 
• It is also an **occasion for the people of Assam to enjoy (bhog kora)** and share in the gifts of nature as a community, and strengthen a sense of identity and belonging.
 
 
 
• **Dussehra**
 
 
• ​Dussehra, also called Dasara or** Vijayadashami, in Hinduism.**
 
• The Festival marks the **triumph of Lord Rama,** an avatar of Vishnu, over the **10-headed demon king Ravana**, who abducted Lord Rama's wife, Sita.

questions.question: Christmas, the annual festival celebrated by the Christian community as a celebration of the birth of Jesus Christ, is celebrated on which of the following date?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** **__**25 December.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Christmas commemorates the birth of Jesus Christ.**
 
• It is celebrated by a majority of **Christians on December 25 in the Gregorian calendar.**
 
• The Holy **Bible does not mention the date of the birth** of Christ.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Roman Christian **historian Sextus Julius Africanus** dated Jesus’s conception to March 25, which, after 9 months, is December 25.
 
• Hence, the birth date was decided.
 
• The **church in Rome** began formally celebrating Christmas on **December 25 in 336, **during the **reign of the emperor Constantine.**

questions.question: The National Commission for Farmers, headed by whom, had suggested that the Minimum Support Price (MSP) for agricultural crops should be at least 50% higher than the weighted average cost of production?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** M.S. Swaminathan.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Swaminathan Commission Report **suggested that the government should raise the **MSP to at least 50%** more than the weighted average cost of production.
 
• It is also known as the** C2+ 50% formula.**
 
• It includes the input cost of capital and the rent on the land (called ‘C2’) to give** farmers 50% returns.**
 
• **M.S. Swaminathan **is also known as The Father of the Green Revolution in India.
 
• He received the** first World Food Prize in 1987** for the introduction of high-yielding wheat and rice varieties to India’s farmers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **MSP(Minimum Support Price)**

 
 
• Minimum Support Price (MSP) is a form of** market intervention by the Government of India** to insure agricultural producers against any sharp fall in farm prices.
 
• The minimum support prices are announced by the Government of India at the beginning of the sowing season for certain crops on the basis of the **recommendations of the Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices (CACP).**
 
• Presently, the government announces minimum support prices for **23 crops.**

questions.question: What is the frequency of ultrasonic waves?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**More than 20 kHz.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Ultrasonic wave is defined as **“inaudible sound with high frequency for humans” **the frequency of which generally **exceeds 20 kHz.**
 
• **Properties of ultrasonic waves:**
 
 
• They can not travel through a vacuum.
 
• They can travel with the speed of sound in a given medium.
 
• They are used for welding also.
 
• They can reflect and refract like light rays.
 
• These waves are used in engineering, medical treatment, etc.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Infrasonic sound: **

 
 
• **​**It has a frequency of** less than 20 Hz** and these are generally produced by sources of a bigger size such as **earthquakes, volcanic eruptions, **etc.
 
• Sound waves with frequencies **below the audible range** are called infrasonic.
 
 
 
• **Audible sound:**
 
 
• It has a **frequency of 20-20000 Hz** since these are sensitive to the human ears.
 
• If the frequency is** greater or less than audible frequency, **the human ear won't be able to sense it.
 
 
 
• **Ultrasonic sound:**
 
 
• It has a frequency** greater than 20000 Hz **and certain creatures such as dogs, cats, and bats can hear this kind of sound.

questions.question: The elections to the Constituent Assembly in India were held in _________.

__
 
• Formation of the constituent assembly

 
 
• ​__Under the Cabinet Mission Plan of 1946, elections were held for the **Constituent Assembly in July 1946.**
 
• The members were elected by the members of the provincial assemblies by the method of a single transferable vote of proportional representation.
 
• In the beginning, there were 389 members. But after the partition of the country into India and Pakistan, the number came down to 299
 __
 
• 229 were from the British Indian provinces while the remaining 70 were from the princely states.
 
 
 
• The seats to the British Indian provinces and princely states were allotted in the proportion of their respective population and were to be divided among Muslims, Sikhs and the rest of the communities.

questions.question: The incident ray, the ray perpendicular to the point of incidence, and the reflected ray all lie________.

• According to the **first law of the reflection** the incident ray, the reflected ray, and the normal at the point of incidence, **lie in the same plane.**
 
• The normal is perpendicular to the plane of reflection.
 
• The **angle of incidence ∠ i is equal to the angle of reflection ∠ r.**
